newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says Russia's economic decline has stopped.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says Russia's economic decline has stopped.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin said on Friday the first year of his second presidential term had been the hardest of his life, but that Russia's industrial decline had been halted and the economy could now start growing.

"The breakthrough has already happened," Yeltsin said in a radio address marking the anniversary of his re-election on July 3, 1996. "That is it. We have reached the point when it is possible for production to go up. The decline has been stopped."

Yeltsin gave no figures and did not say when or by how much the economy would grow. Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Wednesday the economy had already started growing in the first six months of this year.

The 66-year-old president spent most of the first eight months of his second presidential term out of the Kremlin because of health problems, but has reaffirmed his grip on power since undergoing heart surgery last November.

"This year, I think, was the most difficult of my life, but it was also a special, unique one. I could never have imagined that a man of my age could change so much. But that is how it turned out. I can feel how I have changed," he said.
As one of the major changes, Yeltsin cited a newly acquired ability to seek and find compromise with opponents, including the communist-dominated State Duma lower house of parliament.
